title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattentionv2 + fused ops + rotary (rope) optimizations
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: integrate FlashAttention v2 kernels and a set of fused attention operations (QKV+proj fusion, fused rotary/rope transforms) into the serving runtime to reduce per-token compute, improve cache locality, and enable higher continuous-batching throughput. This change also updates the KV-cache layout and scheduler hints so the runtime can pick fused kernels for common sequence lengths and model shapes. Key goals: 1) improve p50/p95 latency for generation workloads; 2) increase token throughput for high-concurrency workloads; 3) reduce peak GPU memory and PCIe traffic when possible; 4) keep compatibility fallback to existing kernels for edge cases.

perf: scheduler: add kernel selection heuristics and runtime hints for continuous batching (scheduler/scheduler.cc)
test: add GPU unit tests and microbenchmarks for fused kernels and new cache layout (tests/perf/bench_attn.py)

docs: release notes and performance guidance (docs/release_notes/35840-attn-kernels.md)

ci_checks: benchmarks: pass (internal perf harness - microbench stable)
release_notes: Performance: integrated FlashAttention v2 and fused QKV+proj and rotary ops; typical improvements observed: ~15% p50 latency reduction and up to 20% throughput increase for batched generation on common model shapes. Default canary rollout; see docs/release_notes/35840-attn-kernels.md for rollout steps and compatibility notes.
perf_summary: Microbenchmarks: GPT-like 3B model with sequence lengths [1,64,256] observed p50 latency reduction: 1->0.86x, 64->0.82x, 256->0.88x; end-to-end token throughput improvement 12-22% depending on batch shape. Memory: peak GPU working set down ~10% for long-context workloads due to fused projections and reduced temporary buffers.
compatibility_notes: Feature is guarded behind runtime flag 'enable_fused_attention'. Old KV-cache layout supported via accessor shim for backward compatibility. Fallback to scalar kernels for unsupported shapes/alignments to preserve correctness. Customers running private installer should update third_party/flashattention submodule and rebuild with CUDA >=12.0 for best performance.
canary_plan: Rollout steps: 1) internal perf canary (10% traffic) for 48h; 2) expand to 50% for 24h if no regressions; 3) full rollout and cherry-pick to release branches. Rollback: set 'enable_fused_attention=false' and redeploy; scripts/rollout_canary.sh included.
testing_notes: Added deterministic GPU unit tests and randomized correctness fuzz tests for fused rotary transformations; added perf harness entries and CI microbenchmarks. Verified against existing evaluation prompts and integration tests with streaming endpoints.
notes_for_ops: Operator guidance included in docs: monitor attn_kernel_fallback_rate metric, per-model latency deltas, and GPU memory headroom. Set auto rollback threshold in Redwood Console to revert canary if p99 latency increases >20% or error rates increase.
